rules.effective_date_basis: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.title: Statewide residential rent increase cap
rules.requirement: For covered residential rental property, an owner may not increase rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the applicable cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower. If the same tenant remains in the unit, rent may not be increased in more than two increments during that 12-month period.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10%; no more than two increases in 12 months for same tenant

coverage.small_owner_exception: Separately alienable residential real property, including a mobilehome, is exempt if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with at least one corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the required written exemption notice is provided.
coverage.other_unresolvable: Exemptions also depend on deed or regulatory affordable-housing restrictions or subsidy agreements, school dormitory ownership and operation, stricter local rent or price control, ADU/JADU status in an owner-occupied two-unit property, and whether the occupant is a homeowner of a mobilehome.
coverage.summary: Applies statewide to residential rental units, including units in mobilehome parks, unless a listed exemption applies such as newer housing, certain affordable housing, school dormitories, stricter local rent-controlled units, qualifying separately alienable homes, owner-occupied duplexes, or mobilehome homeowners.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories owned and operated by higher-education or K-12 institutions; housing subject to valid local rent or price control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years unless the housing is a mobilehome; qualifying separately alienable residential property with required notice and non-corporate/non-REIT ownership; certain owner-occupied two-unit single-structure properties where neither unit is an ADU or JADU; or a homeowner of a mobilehome.
rules.penalty: An owner who demands, accepts, receives, or retains rent above the maximum is liable in a civil action for injunctive relief, excess-rent damages, discretionary reasonable attorney’s fees and costs, and, for willful or oppressive, fraudulent, or malicious conduct, up to treble damages; the Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel may enforce and seek injunctive relief.
rules.interaction: The section excludes housing already subject to valid local rent or price control with lower annual increases and states that it does not expand or limit local authority to regulate rents consistently with Chapter 2.7 commencing with Section 1954.50.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
